title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
why_read: A dense statistical learning theory paper on concentration inequalities for non-independent data, useful mainly to theoretical ML researchers working with dependent data streams.
analysis: This paper derives a new probabilistic bound (a Bernstein-type inequality) for data generated by regenerative processes, which are sequences that periodically reset and are not independent like typical ML theory assumes. It uses this bound to produce generalization guarantees for classifiers trained on such non-independent data, and shows the bound is statistically optimal in certain senses. This is highly technical statistical learning theory work, valuable for researchers studying reinforcement learning or time series under dependence, but not something with immediate applied relevance. The writing is dense and mathematical, aimed at a narrow theoretical audience.
